title: Noah Kahan Wrote a Song for the New Hunger Games Movie!
summary:
Have you ever loved a book series so much that you dreamed of writing a song for the movie? That's exactly what happened to singer Noah Kahan.

Kahan just released a new song called "Draw You Out" for the upcoming Hunger Games film, "Sunrise on the Reaping." The movie is a prequel—a story that takes place before the original trilogy. It follows a young Haymitch Abernathy, who fans know as the mentor in the original books and movies.

Kahan is a huge fan of author Suzanne Collins. He wrote on social media that he's "always wanted to do this" and was inspired by the "tragic yet hopeful story" of Haymitch and his friend Lenore Dove. The song's chorus goes: "I carry you on with me / I promised you I would, and I do."

The song was co-written and produced by Aaron Dessner. The full soundtrack album comes out November 13, and the movie opens in theaters November 20. Other Hunger Games movies had songs by Taylor Swift and Olivia Rodrigo. Now Kahan joins that list!
why_it_matters: It shows that loving something, like a book series or music, can lead to real work later — the things you enjoy now could become your job one day.

background_read: The Hunger Games is a book series by Suzanne Collins (an American author) about a future world where children are forced to fight in a televised contest. The first movie came out in 2012 and made the series famous all over the world.
Big movies often ask famous singers to write a song for them. Taylor Swift wrote "Safe & Sound" for the first Hunger Games movie, and Olivia Rodrigo wrote "Can't Catch Me Now" for a later one.
Aaron Dessner is a musician and producer in the band The National, and he has also made albums with Taylor Swift.
